## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The religion is completed  (`#today-the-religion-is-completed`)

Cited ayat: 5:3

> **5:3** حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَيْتَةُ وَٱلدَّمُ وَلَحْمُ ٱلْخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ وَٱلْمُنْخَنِقَةُ وَٱلْمَوْقُوذَةُ وَٱلْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسْتَقْسِمُوا۟ بِٱلْأَزْلَٰمِ ذَٰلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ ٱلْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن دِينِكُمْ فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَٱخْشَوْنِ ٱلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِى وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلْإِسْلَٰمَ دِينًا فَمَنِ ٱضْطُرَّ فِى مَخْمَصَةٍ غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٍ لِّإِثْمٍ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ

### Claims

**c1** (5:3): The verse says that today those who disbelieved have despaired of the religion of those addressed.

**c2** (5:3): Those addressed are told not to fear them but to fear God.

**c3** (5:3): God says that today He has completed their religion for them, has completed His favour upon them, and has approved Islam as their religion.

### One-minute summary

The verse says that today those who disbelieved have despaired of the religion of those addressed [c1]. They are told not to fear them but to fear God [c2]. God says that today He has completed their religion, completed His favour upon them, and approved Islam as their religion [c3].

### Complete story

The verse says that today those who disbelieved have despaired of the religion of those addressed [c1]. Those addressed are told not to fear them but to fear God [c2].

God says that today He has completed their religion for them, has completed His favour upon them, and has approved Islam as their religion [c3].

### Deep study

The statement has parts: what those who disbelieved have done, what those addressed are told, and what God says He has done [c1][c2][c3]. The verse says 'today' and does not give a date [c1][c3]. It does not say what was completed or in what way, only that the religion and the favour were completed [c3]. The same verse contains other matters, which this draft does not restate [c1].

### Kids mode

God says that today He has completed their religion for them [c3]. God says that today He has completed His favour upon them [c3]. God says that He has approved Islam as their religion, and they are told to fear God [c2][c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the verse sets the fear of God against the fear of those who disbelieved [c2]. Another is that it speaks of completion and favour together and puts both with God [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which day 'today' is, or where it was. The verse gives no date or place.
- Not established: what was completed or how, or what 'despaired of your religion' says about what those who disbelieved had hoped for.
- The same verse also names things made forbidden and a case of need. They are not restated in this chapter, whose subject is the announcement; a scholar should decide whether the page shows the verse whole.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the day, the place and the occasion of the announcement. None is used in the story texts.
